Coffee.extract: A brewed drink from roasted coffee beans. Grown widely in the tropics; associated with cafés, caffeine, and breakfast.

Caffeine.extract: A central nervous system stimulant of the methylxanthine class. Found in coffee, tea, and some soft drinks.

Ethiopia.extract: A country in the Horn of Africa. Often cited in stories about the origin of coffee cultivation.

Breakfast.extract: The first meal of the day. Coffee is a common breakfast drink in many countries.

Stimulant.extract: A class of drugs that increase activity in the brain and body. Includes caffeine and some medicines.

Brazil.extract: The largest country in South America and a major coffee exporter.

Tea.extract: A drink made from Camellia sinensis leaves. Also contains caffeine.

Nervous system.extract: The network of nerve cells that transmits signals in the body. Stimulants act on this system.

Pharmacology.extract: The study of how chemical substances affect living organisms. Includes stimulants and anesthetics.

Africa.extract: A continent. Home to Ethiopia and many other coffee-growing regions.

Arabian Peninsula.extract: A peninsula in West Asia. Coffee drinking spread through the region in the early modern period.

South America.extract: A continent that includes Brazil, Colombia, and other coffee producers.

China.extract: A country in East Asia. Associated with tea more than coffee.

NASA.extract: The United States civil space agency. Ran the Apollo program that landed people on the Moon.

Medicine.extract: The practice of diagnosing and treating disease. Overlaps with pharmacology.

Human body.extract: The physical structure of a human being, including the nervous system.

Sleep.extract: A recurring state of rest. Caffeine is used to postpone it.

Trade.extract: The exchange of goods. Coffee and tea were important early modern commodities.

Ottoman Empire.extract: An empire based in Anatolia. Coffeehouses were a prominent urban institution.

Europe.extract: A continent. Coffee reached European ports via Mediterranean trade.

United States.extract: A country in North America. Created NASA and funded Apollo.

Engineering.extract: The application of science to design. Spacecraft are engineered systems.

Cold War.extract: A geopolitical rivalry after World War II. The space race was one theatre.

Apollo program.extract: NASA program that landed humans on the Moon. Apollo 11 was the first landing.

Moon.extract: Earth's only natural satellite. Site of the Apollo landings.

Neil Armstrong.extract: American astronaut. First person to walk on the Moon, on Apollo 11.

Earth.extract: The planet we live on. The Moon orbits Earth.

Apollo 11.extract: The 1969 NASA mission that first landed humans on the Moon. Crew included Neil Armstrong.
